🚨🇲🇽 <u>On the eve of Sheinbaum's trip to China, the US ambassador posts a trade lecture for Mexico</u>

Two days before President Sheinbaum left for the APEC summit in Shenzhen, US Ambassador Ronald Johnson took to X with an infographic accusing China of "flooding" Mexico with low-cost imports. His numbers: 83% of Mexican exports, about $551 billion, go to the US, versus roughly $10 billion, 2%, to China.

Mexico already decides its own trade policy. It raised tariffs on countries without a trade agreement, China included, in January 2026. It doesn't need an embassy graphic to choose its partners.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Fovissste converts 80,000 UMA-indexed mortgages to fixed pesos at 9%</u>

Starting Nov 16, 80,000 Fovissste home loans denominated in UMA can be restructured: converted to pesos at a fixed 9% rate, with no more annual UMA adjustments and debt write-downs where needed. "There will be no more updates; there will be fixed payments, a fixed rate, a fixed term, and they will be able to pay off their loan," said executive director Jabnely Maldonado Meza (El Economista). In Hidalgo alone, more than 21,000 state workers have already received payoffs, interest forgiveness, balance cuts or restructurings.

🇲🇽📚 Oaxaca's intercultural book fair returns: 120+ free events led by Indigenous and Afro-Mexican voices The second Intercultural Writing and Reading Fair of Oaxaca (FIELO) runs Nov 19-29 in Oaxaca City's historic center. It offers more than 120 free activities and 15 concerts, with 50 exhibitors that include 30 publishers, 10 of them from Oaxaca. Headliners include Zapotec poet Natalia Toledo, Mixtec poet Celerina Patricia Sánchez, Tsotsil writer Mikel Ruiz and Mixe author Mito Reyes, whose novel Kopk Poj moves between Spanish and Ayöök. Governor Salomón Jara launched the fair under the motto "Read, create, transform."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sinaloa Cartel operator arrested in Tijuana, with a US gun pipeline behind him</u>

Federal and Baja California forces arrested José Alberto Leyva Acosta, named as a trusted operator of René and Alfonso Arzate García, "La Rana" and "El Aquiles," who lead the Mayiza faction. According to the Security Cabinet, he ran front businesses in Tijuana to launder money, smuggled people from Tijuana into San Diego and San Ysidro, and kept a network in the United States that supplied guns and stolen vehicles to the cartel. Defensa, Marina, SSPC, Guardia Nacional and FGR carried out the operation using information shared by US Homeland Security Investigations, "under the principle of respect for national sovereignty."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Chiapas restarts temporary jobs for migrants as a new caravan crosses the state</u>

Governor Eduardo Ramírez told the Southern Border Secretariat to restart Chiapas' temporary employment program for migrants in transit, offering "productive activities and an option for dignified work" during their stay. The "Dios con nosotros" caravan left Honduras on Nov 3 and is moving up the Chiapas coast, while Trump threatens Mexico with higher tariffs over caravans. The jobs are not residency and not a ticket to the US. Wages, duration and paperwork rules have not been announced yet.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE flags 45 of 72 election purchases as "high risk" after Taddei's exit</u>

Mexico's electoral institute is falling behind on supplies for the 2027 midterms. As of Nov 10, its Electoral Organization directorate rated 45 of 72 procurement items high-risk and 20 medium-risk. Civic Education flags 10 more, and IT flags two, including supplies for the PREP preliminary count. La Jornada traces the disorder to the last stretch of Guadalupe Taddei's term, which ended with her resignation on Oct 26. The INE's own internal comptroller has already found five companies that faked competition to split 2,461 million pesos in electoral-material contracts for state electoral bodies between 2014 and 2025.

‍FREIGHTWAVES: Borderlands Mexico: Texas cross-border traffic rises by 400 trucks through Saturday pilot November 15, 2026 | 🟢 📰 FreightWaves reports the numbers straight: US-Mexico freight hit $96.3B in September, up 34.2% from a year earlier, and trucks carried $75.4B of it. The extra Saturday hours at Laredo's World Trade Bridge were requested by Mexico's customs agency, ANAM. 🇲🇽 These figures came out the same week Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico. US-Canada freight grew 10.1% over the same period. • "Total U.S.-Mexico freight trade increased 34.2%" • "requested by Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM)"

‍NYT: A Mexican Artist Sang Some of His Hits. Authorities Stopped the Show, Then Arrested Him. November 14, 2026 | 🟡 📰 The NYT's headline and dek treat Gabito Ballesteros's arrest in Querétaro as a free-speech story: the show was stopped over songs that "supposedly glorify cartel culture." 🇲🇽 Milenio and Record report he was held by Mexico's federal prosecutor (FGR) over a firearm (a pistol, two magazines and 34 rounds) and released after about 17 hours. His own team apologized to Querétaro, calling it "an error of judgment." • "supposedly glorify cartel culture" • "renewed a debate over culture and free speech"
